caption: Voronoi: cells like stained glass over the cube, dark cracks between, each cell its own colour
why: Scatter points through space and give every place to its nearest point: you get cells - the pattern of a giraffe's coat, dried mud, foam, stained glass. Voronoi does that for every pixel, in the cube's real space, so the cells run over the edges without a seam.

It answers three ways: the distance to the nearest point (soft round cells), how far from the edge between two cells (the cracks), and a random number per cell (its own colour). Its neighbours: Brick and Checker are regular grids; Noise has no cells; Voronoi is irregular cells.
steps: **pos** is unwired, so it is the pixel's own place in the cube: the cells are three-dimensional and flow over the edges.
**scale** is 1.2: about one cell per unit of the cube's -1..1 box, so two or three cells to a face. **seed** picks the scatter of points - another seed, other cells.
`edge` - 0 on the boundary between cells, larger toward the middle - goes into a **Smoothstep** whose edges are 0 and 0.15: dark on the cracks, lit inside. That is the **Palette**'s brightness.
`id` - one random number for the whole cell - plus a slow clock (**Time** times 0.1) is the palette's index: each cell its own colour, all of them shifting slowly together.

try.label: Smaller cells
try.text: scale 3 (the node's own default): two and a half times the cells each way - a fine mosaic, each cell a few LEDs.

try.label: Different cells
try.text: seed 7: the points are scattered differently, so every cell changes shape and place.

try.label: Wide cracks
try.text: the Smoothstep's second edge at 0.45: the dark spreads far in from each edge, leaving glowing islands in the middle of the cells.
